<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title><jats:p>Suppose <jats:italic>X</jats:italic> is a multidimensional diffusion process. Assume that at time zero the state of <jats:italic>X</jats:italic> is fully observed, but at time <jats:inline-formula><jats:alternatives><jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" mime-subtype="png" mimetype="image" xlink:href="S0001867819000545_inline1.png"/><jats:tex-math>
$T>0$
</jats:tex-math></jats:alternatives></jats:inline-formula> only linear combinations of its components are observed. That is, one only observes the vector <jats:inline-formula><jats:alternatives><jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" mime-subtype="png" mimetype="image" xlink:href="S0001867819000545_inline2.png"/><jats:tex-math>
$L X_T$
</jats:tex-math></jats:alternatives></jats:inline-formula> for a given matrix <jats:italic>L</jats:italic>. In this paper we show how samples from the conditioned process can be generated. The main contribution of this paper is to prove that guided proposals, introduced in [35], can be used in a unified way for both uniformly elliptic and hypo-elliptic diffusions, even when <jats:italic>L</jats:italic> is not the identity matrix. This is illustrated by excellent performance in two challenging cases: a partially observed twice-integrated diffusion with multiple wells and the partially observed FitzHugh–Nagumo model.</jats:p>
title: Simulation of elliptic and hypo-elliptic conditional diffusions
